articles.title: Samay Raina in soup again over remarks on people from Bihar, Kashmiri Pandits: 'They get publicity for free'
articles.summary: MUMBAI: Comedian Samay Raina released another episode of India's Got Latent, Season 2, on Friday, with parts of the show later circulating on social m.
articles.body: MUMBAI: Comedian Samay Raina released another episode of India's Got Latent, Season 2, on Friday, with parts of the show later circulating on social media.The episode has drawn attention over alleged remarks about people from Bihar and Kashmiri Pandits made during an interaction involving Raina and stand-up comedian Sharon Verma.The exchange began when Samay introduced Sharon to the audience in his usual style, making a joke about her Bihar background. He said, “She is from Bihar. She is so Bihari; she thinks ‘ebola’ means someone said something.”Sharon responded with a joke targeting Samay’s Kashmiri roots, telling him, “Samay is so Kashmiri; he loves getting stoned.”Samay continued the banter, adding, “Sharon Verma is a Bihari who came to Mumbai in search of a job. Just Bihari things.”Sharon then said, “At least, I left my state by my choice.”'Cannot be treated as subjects of ridicule'BJP MLA Ram Kadam criticised the alleged remarks and said they were made for publicity."There are certain forces in society that deliberately make controversial statements simply to gain publicity. Their sole objective is to become famous. We need to understand that the deities of Sanatan Hinduism and Kashmiri Pandits cannot be treated as subjects of ridicule.""Someone cannot deliberately do something offensive and then simply apologize afterwards. In the meantime, they get the publicity they wanted across the country for free," he added further again.Kashmiri Pandit's react to remarksReacting to the alleged remarks, a Kashmiri Pandit said, "Look, there is no need to give too much importance to whatever conversation Samay Raina had.""It was a comedy show, and it can be called a comedy show. If I am a Kashmiri Pandit, I have the right to travel anywhere in the world; it is our fundamental right.""Similarly, if someone from Bihar goes to Bombay, it is their fundamental right. They can go anywhere in the country and live anywhere for employment or any other reason.""Now, regarding the conversation they had with each other, when you go to a comedy show, jokes keep happening. One should not take it personally, nor should it be given so much importance as to who said what to whom," he added.Another Kashmiri Pandit said, "There is a comedian named Samay Raina. He is a good man. You have seen him. We respect him and we are proud of him.""Comedians say such things, but there are other things behind them. You talked about migration but migration did not happen. They were forced to migrate.""I said that the way a comedian talks is different. It depends on the way a person thinks and how he takes it," he added.'Absuing is talent?'The episode also featured actress and television personality Archana Puran Singh and social media personality Orhan Awatramani, popularly known as Orry, on the panel.During the show, Raina also took a dig at Archana while speaking to a contestant.A contestant named AR Tiwari performed Bhojpuri shayari on the show. When Raina asked him what he did apart from shayari, the contestant said he also danced, vlogged and rapped.Raina then used the mention of vlogging to joke about Archana, who regularly shares family vlogs.He told the contestant, "Did you say vlog? Vlogging doesn't need talent".Archana was quick to respond.Giving Raina a sharp comeback, she said, "gaaliyan dena talent hai? (abusing is talent)."Her response was met with cheers from the audience, while Raina did not immediately have a comeback.The latest episode comes amid renewed attention on India's Got Latent, with clips from the show frequently being shared and discussed on social media.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Mumbai | Silver Rate in Mumbai | Bank Holidays in Mumbai | Public Holidays in Mumbai | Mumbai AQI | Weather in Mumbai | Petrol Price in Mumbai | Diesel Price in Mumbai | CNG Price in Mumbai | LPG Price in MumbaiStay updated with the latest Mumbai news. articles.title: In 2017, US government introduced 60-day grace period for H-1B visa workers; 9 years later DHS wants to end it; here's the status update
articles.summary: Tech News News: For nearly nine years, foreign workers in the US who lost their jobs have had a 60-day window to find a new employer or change their immigration statu.
articles.body: For nearly nine years, foreign workers in the US who lost their jobs have had a 60-day window to find a new employer or change their immigration status. Now, that protection may be removed. According to a Bloomberg Law report, a proposal from the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) to end the 60-day grace period has cleared a key White House review, moving it closer to becoming public. If approved, the proposal could have a major impact on H-1B visa holders, including thousands of Indian professionals, who are among the biggest users of the visa programme. However, the rule has not taken effect yet, and its final details are still not public.What is the 60-day grace period for H-1B workersThe grace period was introduced in 2017. It allows certain foreign workers and their dependents to remain in the US for up to 60 consecutive days after their employment ends, provided their authorised stay has not expired. During this period, workers can look for a new job, find another employer willing to sponsor them, or apply to change their immigration status.The rule covers several visa categories, including H-1B, L-1, O-1, E-1, E-2, E-3, H-1B1 and TN visa holders, along with eligible dependents. The provision has been particularly important for H-1B workers who face sudden layoffs, giving them limited time to make decisions without having to immediately leave the country.What could happen if the grace period is removedIf the proposal is finalised as described, foreign workers whose jobs end before their authorised stay expires could face much tougher rules. They and their dependents could generally be required to leave the US immediately after losing their jobs. Changing employers or immigration status from within the country could also become more difficult unless US Citizenship and Immigration Services uses its discretion to forgive a lapse in status.The possible change comes at a time when job cuts and uncertainty in the technology sector have already raised concerns among skilled foreign workers.Why the move matters to Indian H-1B workersIndian nationals are among the biggest beneficiaries of the H-1B programme. They accounted for 71% of successful H-1B applicants in fiscal year 2024, according to the information provided.The proposal could therefore have a significant impact on Indian professionals and their families living in the US. The Indian-American population in the country is estimated at around 5.2 million.Former White House adviser Ajay Jain Bhutoria criticised the proposal and called for the grace period to be extended to 180 days instead."Eliminating the 60-day grace period is both inhumane and unworkable. When a high-skilled worker faces a sudden termination, 60 days is already dangerously short. Stripping away this protection entirely leaves thousands of law-abiding individuals with zero time to wrap up their lives,” said Bhutoria.He also said families could face serious disruption if workers are forced to leave immediately after losing their jobs.What happens nextThe next major step is the proposal's publication in the Federal Register. That will reveal exactly what DHS is proposing and start the public comment process before any final decision is made. For now, the key takeaway for H-1B workers is that the 60-day grace period remains in place. The White House review is an important step forward for the proposal, but it is not the final rule.The development is said to be part of a broader set of proposed policy changes affecting the H-1B programme, making the next steps closely watched by foreign workers, US employers and immigration experts alike.Get the latest technology news and updates. articles.title: From 200 km to 500 km: How long-range missiles are rewriting the rules of air combat
articles.summary: International News: A decade ago, the notion of striking an airborne target at 200 kilometres was considered a rare feat, more a matter of chance than certainty. Today, t.
articles.body: A decade ago, the notion of striking an airborne target at 200 kilometres was considered a rare feat, more a matter of chance than certainty. Today, the envelope of air-to-air missile engagements has expanded dramatically, with systems now promising ranges of 400 to 500 kilometres, and in some cases even more. This transformation is reshaping aerial warfare, shifting the emphasis from close-in dogfights to long-range denial of critical enablers such as airborne early warning aircraft, tankers and electronic warfare platforms.China’s PL-17, designed to neutralise high-value assets, is reported to reach nearly 400 kilometres, while Russia’s R-37M, capable of Mach 6 speeds, has been deployed on MiG-31 and Su-35 fighters with ranges around 300 kilometres. Europe’s Meteor, powered by a throttleable ramjet, sustains flight well beyond 150 kilometres, giving partner air forces a decisive edge in beyond-visual-range combat. India’s Astra programme, initially fielded with ranges of 110 to 160 kilometres, is now being expanded into longer-range variants, with reports suggesting capabilities approaching 300 kilometres. For the Indian Air Force, the integration of such systems into future platforms like the AMCA will be critical to maintaining parity with peer competitors.The United States has now unveiled its most ambitious programme yet, one that could redraw the rules of aerial combat for decades. Announced at a naval aviation symposium, the AIM-424 Long Range Air-to-Air Missile, also referred to as Malice, is being developed to ensure American forces retain the edge in what planners describe as first look, first shot, first kill engagements. Manufactured by Raytheon, Malice stretches 13.5 feet, weighs 680 kilograms, and employs a two-stage solid-propellant rocket motor to achieve a stated range exceeding 250 nautical miles, or roughly 463 kilometres. It is designed to arm both current and future fighters, from the F/A-18E/F Super Hornet and F-35C to the sixth-generation F/A-XX, giving naval aviators a weapon tailored for today’s air wings and tomorrow’s. Where Malice fits alongside the AIM-174B, adapted from the Navy’s ship-launched SM-6 interceptor, remains to be seen, but the Pentagon’s ambition is clear: to eventually field air-to-air weapons capable of reaching nearly a thousand miles, a capability seen as essential to counter adversary anti-access systems and to dominate extended kill chains.From the era of 200 kilometre “lucky shots” to today’s 500 kilometre sightlines, air combat has become a contest of reach, precision and denial. The trajectory points towards even greater ranges in the coming decade, demanding not only advances in propulsion but also robust sensor networks and data links to cue missiles accurately at extreme distances. The decisive battles of the future may well be fought long before opposing fighters ever come within visual range.

articles.title: China tests GJ-21 stealth UAV as Sichuan drone carrier enters final sea trials
articles.summary: International News: China flight-tested its GK-21 stealth attack drone this month as the 40,000-tonne Sichuan, the amphibious assault ship designed to launch the drone, e.
articles.body: China flight-tested its GK-21 stealth attack drone this month as the 40,000-tonne Sichuan, the amphibious assault ship designed to launch the drone, entered its final sea trials.According to the South China Morning Post, three recent videos posted on Chinese social media showed the GJ-21 flying over a highway service area in Huludao, a city in Liaoning province in northeastern China.The GJ-21, the naval variant of the GJ-11 stealth attack drone, was first unveiled at China’s Victory Day parade in September last year and has made only rare public appearances since.Computer-generated footage aired by state broadcaster CCTV in July showed the drone being launched from the Type 076 Sichuan, Beijing’s most advanced amphibious assault ship and the world’s first drone carrier.In its July broadcast, CCTV quoted an expert as saying that the Sichuan had entered its final testing phase.The Sichuan is the world’s only amphibious assault ship equipped with an electromagnetic catapult system and is expected to launch both crewed and uncrewed fixed-wing aircraft, including the GJ-21 drone, as well as helicopters.Also on Thursday, satellite imagery shared by X user MT Anderson appeared to show the Sichuan, along with two Type 052 destroyers and three Type 054 frigates, off the Qingdao naval base on August 25. The base is the headquarters of the PLA Navy’s Northern Theatre Command.With a full-load displacement of more than 40,000 tonnes, the Sichuan is designed to transport landing craft, troops, armoured vehicles and aircraft for amphibious operations. It is also expected to be among Beijing’s key assets in any potential conflict over Taiwan.The PLA Navy is expected to take delivery of the warship by the end of this year.

articles.title: Watch: Family watches in horror from balcony as strong floodwaters wash away everything but their house
articles.summary: South Asia News: A family watched in horror from the balcony of a green-painted house as raging floodwaters swept through the area, carrying debris and tearing apart b.
articles.body: A family watched in horror from the balcony of a green-painted house as raging floodwaters swept through the area, carrying debris and tearing apart buildings around them in one of Nepal’s deadliest disasters in years.Video footage of the house went viral after showing the family apparently trapped inside as muddy, fast-moving water surged around the building. Nearby structures were swept away by the force of the flood, while debris could be seen being carried through the streets.Yet in a later video, the green house was still standing, surrounded by torrents of floodwater.The floods have killed at least 626 people in Nepal, according to local authorities, while 2,426 people remain missing. More than 3,700 people have been rescued so far. The disaster has also claimed seven lives in neighbouring Tibet, where more than 550 people are reported missing.Heavy rain returned to parts of northern Nepal on Saturday, hampering rescue operations and raising fears of further flooding. In Trishuli, the military warned residents of possible additional surges, while teams remained on alert over a lake formed by water and debris after a glacier collapse near the Nepal-China border.At the Upper Trishuli-1 hydropower project in Rasuwa district, rescuers continued searching for more than 100 people believed to be trapped inside a tunnel filled with up to 1.5 metres of mud. Rescue teams have used ropes and baskets to reach survivors, but the operation has been made harder by the thick mud and limited helicopter landing areas.As helicopters resumed flights in Nuwakot after bad weather disrupted operations, soldiers evacuated survivors, including babies and elderly people, while others delivered clothes, rice, noodles and other supplies.In Kathmandu, the scale of the loss was becoming clearer as desperate families gathered outside hospitals searching for missing relatives. Photographs and contact details of missing people covered walls, while officials displayed images of unidentified bodies in the hope that someone would recognise them.At a hospital help desk, security official Gajendra Rawat said about 1,600 missing people had been registered.“I came here with the hope that I might find him,” Dil Maya Lama said while searching for her missing brother. “There is no information about him.”Catch the latest World News and Live updates.
